label: e1a12-ai1135-tex1140-30y
_why: TEXTILE'S MERGED HOST AT ITS OWN COST, a 30-year probe (user-ruled 2026-10-03: 'Go with the host cost, run a 30-year probe' — the first lever of the two vectors 'increase obsolescence for specifically textile' / 'boost USA', FINDINGS F211 §4). Book config/mod_config.e1a12-ai1135-tex1140-artmerge.json = the arm's book e1a12-ai1135-artmerge regenerated through its own merge step with `make_merge_config --host-cost textile:own`: the Sewing Machines host (building_textile_mill_sewing_machines, which also runs Electric Sewing Machines from electrical_capacitors) costs its own e2's 1,140 construction points instead of the merge midpoint 1,571; its ai_value stays the midpoint 3,873. Field diff against the arm's book: that one building_cost and the _merge records, nothing else (proven); tree twin = the arm's (with Conveyors before Compression Ignition, which gates nothing before 1900). WHY: F211 found textile's e1 (Dye Workshops) survives because the frontier is under-built — 192 shortlist Sewing Machines levels at 1936 against the canon's 704, clothes ~0.85 of base against ~0.70 — and that frontier returns ~1.5 £ a week per construction point at 1866 at 1,571 points (≈ 2.1 at 1,140) against the mines' 1.3-1.5 and logging's 1.8-2.5. Under §10.92 the lever is a recipe/cost one, not a desire. One run.

Same tags, metrics, quarterly autosaves; dump dates as before plus 1865.1.1 (one more price read; the shared dates stay comparable). _questions.Q1: Is it broken? Init marker, no error naming our files, no crash loop, no stall (world GDP at 1865 under 0.8 of vanilla's median), no industry dead and no market left with a token (health_vs_ref.mjs at 1866 against the n3 seeds), no single building family dominating a major's construction queue.
_questions.Q2: THE FRONTIER: shortlist and world Sewing Machines levels at 1850 / 1860 / 1866 (textile_luxury.mjs --runs), its profit per staffed level and per construction point (return_per_point.mjs), against the arm's six seeds.
_questions.Q3: THE OLD RUNG: Dye Workshops levels, staffing and profit at 1866, and the clothes price in the shortlist's markets at 1850 / 1860 / 1865.
_questions.Q4: WHERE CONSTRUCTION GOES: the US private queue's textile + furniture share and raw + infrastructure share in 1846-56 and 1856-66 (us_construction_windows.mjs — F204's signature), and misplaced capital 1846-56 / 1856-66 (misplaced_capital.mjs).
_questions.Q5: World and shortlist GDP at 1850 / 1860 / 1865 against the arm's seeds; play time 1836 -> 1866 against the earlier probe.

_predictions.Q1: not broken: one building's cost moved, nothing else
_predictions.Q2: more Sewing Machines by 1866 than the arm's median seed: shortlist 20-60 levels (the arm's six seeds 3-41, median 14); a reading above 41 is outside every reference seed and reads as the lever working; one inside 3-41 says a thirty-year seed cannot tell (the frontier's divergence from the canon came after 1880, F211). Profit per staffed level a little below the arm's £2,100-2,400 if more of it is built (the clothes price falls), still ≥ 1.5 £/wk per point
_predictions.Q3: Dye Workshops levels at 1866 inside the arm's 104-133 (the old rung's death is a post-1880 matter, F211) but fewer NEW ones 1856-66; clothes at 1865 a few points below the arm's 1860 readings where the frontier grew
_predictions.Q4: misplaced capital 1856-66 not above the arm's 15-20% (the cheaper frontier is a better use of capital, not a worse one); the US textile + furniture share 1856-66 likely up from the n3's 0-23% — up to ~30% reads as the lever reaching the US; above the earlier probe's 47% flags F204's capture returning
_predictions.Q5: world GDP at 1865 inside 0.93-1.03 of vanilla; play time within 10% of the earlier probe's

_stop_rule: a probe: no stop watcher, no end state for the register to judge. Clearly broken = Q1 fails. What follows (a century 2+1, more probes, or nothing) is PROPOSED to the user, not launched.
_cost: 1 run x 1836 -> 1866, about 40-45 minutes plus build and harvest
